parameters.question: Decision tree classifier for drug response (responder vs non-responder) from SNPs and clinical features, using a 70/30 train-test split. Compare the top 10 feature importances. At least 7 of the 10 highest-ranked features must overlap with the reference set. Importance scores for overlapping features must be within +/-0.05. Row order and column labels may differ.

files.strategy_reasoning: The 70/30 split makes the task stochastic, but the output is a small table of about 10 feature-importance values. The guideline asks for feature overlap and a ±0.05 score tolerance, so the values should be compared one by one with approximate matching rather than with summary. Approximate matching also handles the allowed differences in row order and column labels.

align_plan.reasoning: Both tables list features in long format, so no transpose is needed. The reference's Feature and Importance columns map directly to the candidate columns with the same names. The candidate's extra columns, Rank and CV_Mean_Importance, are not in the reference and are left out. Rows are matched on the Feature name, a categorical identifier, rather than on importance scores, which are computed values. The guideline says row order may differ and judges top-10 overlap as a set, so row order does not matter and permutation checking is on. Some feature names differ in encoding: the reference has 'Disease_Stage_Stage_IV' (one-hot encoded) and the candidate has 'Disease_Stage'. These rows will not match exactly, which matters for scoring but does not change the structural alignment.

column_configs.name: Importance
column_configs.reasoning: The guideline needs importance scores within ±0.05 absolute for overlapping top features. Reference values are about 0.03–0.09, so ±0.05 is roughly 60% or more of each value. An RAE cutoff of 0.6 matches the absolute tolerance for the larger, top-ranked features. Importances are always non-negative, so signs are compared as-is.

comparison_plan.overall_reasoning: The only column the reference and candidate share, apart from the ID, is Importance (float64). 'Feature' is the alignment ID, so it is not compared. The candidate's extra columns, Rank and CV_Mean_Importance, are not in the reference and are left out. The guideline asks for importance scores within ±0.05 absolute on overlapping features. Feature overlap is already handled by alignment on Feature, and NaN rows show features missing from one side's top set. Importance is compared with RAE (relative absolute error). Because an absolute tolerance of ±0.05 has to be expressed as a relative one, the cutoff is set at 0.6. Reference importances are mostly about 0.035–0.085, so ±0.05 equals a relative error of roughly 0.6–1.4. A cutoff of 0.6 is a middle value that matches ±0.05 for the larger, top-ranked features and stays fairly strict. Importances are non-negative, so compare_abs is false.

parameters.question: Compare decision tree test accuracy for drug response prediction (70/30 split). The test accuracy value must be within +/-0.05 of the reference; column naming and label formatting may differ.

files.strategy_reasoning: The random 70/30 split makes the task stochastic, but the output is a small results table built around one test accuracy value. That calls for a value-by-value comparison, with the guideline's ±0.05 tolerance absorbing run-to-run noise and approximate alignment handling differences in column names and labels.

align_plan.reasoning: The two tables have the same shape (1x2) and identical column names (Metric, Value), so the columns map one-to-one and no transpose is needed. Each table has a single row holding the test accuracy. The metric labels differ only in formatting ('Test Accuracy' vs 'Test_Accuracy'), and the guideline says label formatting may differ. Keying on Metric would therefore fail on an exact string match, so the plan uses positional alignment (id_columns=[]). With only one row, row order, sorting and permutation checks don't matter. The comparison should check Value within the ±0.05 tolerance.

column_configs.name: Metric
column_configs.reasoning: This column is only a label ('Test Accuracy' vs 'Test_Accuracy'). The guideline says naming and label formatting may differ, so it is not scored.

column_configs.name: Value
column_configs.reasoning: Test accuracy must be within ±0.05 (absolute) of the reference value of 0.65. As a relative tolerance that is 0.05/0.65 ≈ 0.0769.

comparison_plan.overall_reasoning: The only thing that matters here is the test accuracy value. The guideline allows it to differ from the reference by up to ±0.05 (absolute), and says naming and label formatting may differ. So the Metric label column is ignored. The Value column is compared with relative absolute error (RAE). An absolute margin of 0.05 on a reference of 0.65 works out to a relative tolerance of 0.05/0.65 ≈ 0.0769. The candidate's 0.7417 is 0.0917 away from the reference, an RAE of about 0.141, so it is outside the tolerance and should fail.
